verses.1: On that day, King Ahasuerus gave to Queen Esther the house of Haman, the adversary of the Jews, and Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told him what Haman had done to her.
verses.2: The king removed his signet ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. Esther then set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
verses.3: Esther continued speaking before the king, and fell at his feet, weeping, and begged him to remove the evil of Haman the Agagite and his plot that he had devised against the Jews.
verses.4: The king stretched out the golden scepter to Esther. Esther rose and stood before the king.
verses.5: She said, "If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in your sight, and if this matter is good in the king's eyes and I am pleasing in his sight, then let it be written to reverse the letters of Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, who wrote to destroy the Jews in all the king's provinces.
verses.6: How could I bear to see such evil happen to my people, or see the destruction of my birthright?"
verses.7: King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, "Indeed, I have given the house of Haman to Esther, and let him be hanged on the gallows, for he laid his hand against the Jews."
verses.8: "But you, write to the Jews in the name of the king, as it seems good to you, and seal it with the king's signet ring, for the writing that is sealed in the name of the king and with the king's signet ring cannot be reversed."
verses.9: So the scribes of the king were summoned at that time, in the third month, which is the month of Sivan, on the twenty-third day of it. Mordecai dictated to the Jews and to the satraps, the governors, and the leaders of the provinces, from Hodu to Kush, seventy and two provinces. He dictated to each province in its writing, to each people in its language, and to the Jews in their writing and in their language.
verses.10: He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed it with the king's signet ring, and sent letters by mounted couriers on swift horses that belonged to the king's royal couriers.
verses.11: The king gave to the Jews, who were in every city and town, the right to gather and stand for their lives, to destroy, to kill, and to annihilate every force of the people and province that sought to harm them, from boy to girl, and to plunder their goods.
verses.12: On one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar.
verses.13: The writing was to be given out as a decree in every province and province, made clear to all the peoples, and for the Jews to be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
verses.14: The couriers, the mounted royal couriers, went out hurriedly and were breathless in carrying out the king's word, and the decree was given out in the citadel of Susa.
verses.15: Mordecai went out from before the king in royal robes of blue and white, with a large golden crown, and a linen and purple robe. The city of Susa rejoiced and was glad.
verses.16: For the Jews it was a light and joy, gladness and honor.
verses.17: In every province and province, in every city and city, wherever the king's word and his decree reached, there was joy and gladness for the Jews, a feast and a good day. And many of the peoples became Jews, because the fear of the Jews had fallen upon them.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "house of Haman" is a metaphor for Haman's estate or possessions.
- v. 3: "weaving" of Haman's plot is not in the Hebrew text; the Hebrew simply refers to his plan.
- v. 5: "the son of Hammedatha" is a title or name associated with Haman and is preserved as such.
- v. 13: "made clear to all the peoples" reflects the Hebrew "גָּלוּי לְכָל־הָעַמִּים" which is best understood as "revealed to all the peoples."
- v. 14: "citadel of Susa" is a contextual rendering of "שׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה," where "בִּירָה" can mean "citadel" or "fortress."
- v. 15: "royal robes of blue and white" is a contextual rendering of "בִּלְבוּשׁ מַלְכוּת תְּכֵלֶת וָחוּר," where "תְּכֵלֶת" is blue and "חוּר" is white or perhaps "linen."
